context: The prompt requests implementation of rationale field functionality for editing in the Web UI. The technical design answers are stored in .rdd-instance/specifications/technical-design.json where each answer can have an optional 'rationale' field. The Web UI Technical Design page already supports editing answers, but it's unclear whether the rationale functionality is already implemented or needs to be added.

questions.question-text: What is the current state of rationale field support in the Technical Design page?

options.label: Rationale field is not implemented at all - need to add UI controls, backend API, and data persistence
options.pros: Complete implementation from scratch ensures consistency and proper integration

options.label: Rationale field exists in data model but UI is missing - only need to add UI controls and wire to existing API
options.pros: Less effort, backend already handles persistence
options.cons: Need to verify backend compatibility first

options.label: Rationale field is already fully implemented - just needs testing and documentation
options.cons: May not address user's actual need if feature already exists

questions.recommendation-rationale: Based on TR-0189 which specifies that technical-design.json answers include an 'optional rationale field', the data model already supports rationale. The question is whether the Web UI provides input controls for it.

user-selection.value: You should explore the code and verify if it is implemented and how

questions.question-text: Where should the rationale input field appear in the Technical Design page UI?

options.label: As a separate collapsible section below each question after an answer is selected
options.pros: Keeps the interface clean, rationale is optional so it doesn't clutter the form, progressive disclosure improves UX
options.cons: Requires extra click to access, might be overlooked by users

options.label: Always visible below the answer options for every question
options.pros: Immediately visible, no interaction needed, encourages adding rationale
options.cons: Takes up more space, makes form look cluttered when rationale is not needed

options.label: In a modal dialog that opens when clicking an 'Add Rationale' button
options.pros: Doesn't take permanent screen space, focused editing experience
options.cons: Extra clicks required, context switching between form and modal

options.label: As an inline textarea that appears only after an answer is selected
options.pros: Balances visibility with space efficiency, natural flow from answer to rationale
options.cons: Field appears/disappears based on selection state which might be confusing

questions.recommendation-rationale: Showing the rationale field inline after answer selection provides good UX balance - it's visible when relevant, doesn't clutter the form when no answer is selected, and maintains context without requiring modals or extra clicks.

questions.question-text: How should rationale be persisted to the backend?

options.label: Automatically save rationale on blur (when user clicks away from the textarea)
options.pros: No manual save needed, consistent with prompt.md auto-save behavior, prevents data loss
options.cons: More frequent API calls, could save incomplete thoughts

options.label: Save rationale together with the answer when answer is selected or changed
options.pros: Fewer API calls, rationale and answer saved atomically, simpler state management
options.cons: Rationale changes might not be saved if user doesn't change answer

options.label: Require explicit 'Save' button for rationale
options.pros: User has full control, can edit without worrying about premature saves
options.cons: Risk of forgetting to save, inconsistent with auto-save pattern used elsewhere

options.label: Debounced auto-save after 2 seconds of typing inactivity plus save on blur
options.pros: Matches prompt.md pattern, balances responsiveness with API efficiency, saves incomplete work
options.cons: Most complex to implement, might save incomplete rationale text

questions.recommendation-rationale: Auto-save on blur is simple to implement and provides good UX - it saves when the user moves to another field, preventing data loss without requiring explicit save actions. This is less complex than debounced auto-save but still automatic.

questions.question-text: Should rationale be displayed in the category sidebar or question list views?

options.label: Show rationale icon indicator for questions that have rationale, with tooltip preview on hover
options.pros: Provides quick visibility of which questions have rationale without cluttering the view
options.cons: Requires additional UI elements and hover interactions

options.label: Don't show rationale in list views - only show when editing the specific question
options.pros: Simpler UI, keeps focus on answers, rationale is details-level information
options.cons: No way to know which questions have rationale without opening each one

options.label: Show truncated rationale text (first 50 chars) in the question list
options.pros: Full visibility of rationale at a glance
options.cons: Makes list view very dense, harder to scan, truncation might be misleading

questions.recommendation-rationale: Rationale is supplementary detail that's most useful during editing. Keeping list views focused on questions and answers makes them easier to scan, and rationale can be viewed when expanding the specific question.
